articles.title: Expert at proving lies as truth: Delhi PWD Minister blames AAP as police flag Barapullah Phase-III errors
articles.description: New Delhi, Oct 7 (IANS) Delhi Public Works Department (PWD) Minister Parvesh Verma on Wednesday blamed the previous Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government for the traffic problems being witnessed on the newly opened Barapullah Phase-III corridor, saying the project was planned and designed during its tenure and that the present government is now working on measures to rectify the shortcomings. The Barapullah Phase-III stretch, which was opened last month, has witnessed slow-moving traffic and congestion due to several design-related shortcomings. Verma said the department has held discussions on both immediate and long-term measures suggested by the Delhi Traffic Police, which has also written to the PWD flagging various problems on the corridor. Addressing a press conference, Verma said the government had also taken note of the traffic situation immediately after the flyover was inaugurated and was concerned about the congestion witnessed on the stretch. Custom Ad: Multiplex "Immediately after the inauguration of the Barapullah Phase-III flyover, especially the Aam Aadmi Party and all the Opposition leaders got ready and jumped into the issue. They are making a lot of noise. We saw that from the very next day, there was so much traffic movement there that the entire area appeared to be in a state of congestion. This was concerning for us as well," he said. However, the Minister said the Opposition had repeatedly raised questions over the design of the corridor without acknowledging that the design had been approved during AAP government's tenure in Delhi. Verma said the project timeline clearly showed that the design had been finalised in 2014-15, when the AAP government was in power, and that key decisions regarding the number of lanes and other aspects of the flyover were taken at that time. "The Aam Aadmi Party is an expert at proving lies as truth. There is no match for them when it comes to presenting any lie as the truth. The Barapullah Phase-III flyover project began in 2015. That means its design had already been approved in 2014-2015, when the Aam Aadmi Party government had come to power in Delhi. The entire design was approved during their tenure. How many lanes the flyover would have -- all of this was decided by them," Verma said. The Delhi PWD Minister said he inspected the Barapullah flyover shortly after the BJP government assumed office in February 2025 and claimed that a substantial portion of the construction work had already been completed by then. "298 pillars had to be erected for this flyover. When we came to power, 80 per cent of the work was done. Of the 298 pillars, 288 had already been erected," he said. Verma also outlined the financial history of the project, saying its initial estimate was prepared in 2014-15 at Rs 1,057 crore, while the company that subsequently took up the construction work submitted a tender for Rs 964 crore. "The work started on April 28, 2015 and was supposed to be completed within 30 months, that is, by October 27, 2017. However, we completed this work just a week before. From 2017 to 2026... This work was delayed for nine years. So much of taxpayers' and the government's money was wasted," he said. The Minister also alleged that several additional payments were made to the contractor before the BJP government came to power and that the contractor later approached arbitration under a clause included in the contract. "The first escalation to the contractor was Rs 36.66 crore before our government came to power. The second escalation's payment was Rs 39.85 crore, again before our government. Then that contractor went to arbitration because this contract had an arbitration clause. During this, on September 29, 2021, the contractor was awarded Rs 44 crore," he said. Verma said there were other instances in which the AAP government had made payments running into crores to the contractor in connection with arbitration proceedings. Questioning the design of the flyover, the minister said the corridor should have been planned with future traffic requirements in mind. "If we are seeing a traffic jam situation there today, was (AAP chief Arvind) Kejriwal's vision so limited that on one side there is the DND Flyway, which is twice as wide, and on the other side is the Delhi-Meerut Expressway, whose width is also twice as much? You designed a flyover in 2015 where there is no space constraint, over the Yamuna, and still made it only two lanes on each side," Verma said. He questioned why a project involving such a large expenditure was not designed keeping the expected growth in traffic and population over several decades in mind. "Was the Delhi government spending Rs 1,000 crore of public money in 2015 to build it only for two years? Today, whenever you build any building or any flyover, you build it keeping the next 50 to 100 years in mind. There is a traffic study to assess how much traffic and population are there... Accordingly, you decide its size," he said. Custom Ad: Multiplex Verma further alleged that the AAP government was responsible not only for approving the design but also for various technical and financial decisions linked to the project. "The entire design was approved by the AAP government, the technical qualification, tender, Rs 600 crore extra payment -- all this was done during the AAP government. And now, they make a video blaming us," he said. At the same time, Verma said the Delhi government was taking steps to address the traffic congestion and improve the functioning of the newly opened corridor. He said a new U-turn, the possibility of adding another traffic lane, modifications at important merging points and discussions with Google for real-time traffic information were among the measures being considered. He said commuters could start seeing improvements within the next 10 to 15 days, as the PWD was already working on measures recommended by the Delhi Traffic Police and its consultants. The announcement came after the Delhi Traffic Police wrote to the PWD seeking changes to the corridor to improve traffic flow. Among the measures suggested by the police are a redesign of the merger near Sundial Park and the creation of a dedicated U-turn near Gurudwara Bala Sahib. The Traffic Police has also flagged a mismatch between lane capacity and the geometry of the merger as one of the major factors contributing to congestion on the newly opened stretch. The department has sought changes to improve the movement of vehicles and prevent bottlenecks at critical points. Built for Rs 1,635 crore, the Barapullah Phase-III flyover connects Mayur Vihar Phase-1 on Noida Link Road with Sarai Kale Khan on Ring Road. The corridor merges with the existing Barapullah network and forms part of a continuous 10-kilometre signal-free stretch extending up to the AIIMS roundabout. --IANS sd/vd

articles.title: Delhi HC directs govt to decide in 6 months on SOP for body cameras for police, RAF
articles.description: New Delhi, Oct 7 (IANS) The Delhi High Court on Wednesday directed the government to treat a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking mandatory use of body-worn cameras by Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force (RAF) personnel deployed for crowd control and protest management duties as a representation. A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Arun Bhardwaj directed the government to take a decision within six months on the framing of a standard operating procedure (SOP) concerning the use of body-worn cameras by police and RAF personnel during protests and crowd-control operations. The High Court passed the order while disposing of a PIL filed by advocate Chahat Raghav in the aftermath of the July 2026 demonstrations at Jantar Mantar involving the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and climate activist Sonam Wangchuk. Senior advocate Akhil Sibal, appearing for the petitioner, submitted that the Delhi Police's existing framework relies on third-person videographers positioned along the periphery and does not provide an adequate mechanism for contemporaneous recording of actions by personnel deployed for crowd control. Custom Ad: Multiplex He argued that the availability of technology for body-worn cameras could go a long way in ensuring transparency and fixing accountability during crowd-control operations. "If technology is available, it can go a long way in fixing accountability whenever required. It is different from facial recognition where there are concerns of surveillance," the senior counsel argued. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the Centre, submitted that the petition could be treated as a representation and that a decision would be communicated within six months. Referring to a Supreme Court judgment and the Delhi High Court rules, ASG Sharma said that a representation was required to be made to the authorities concerned before invoking the PIL jurisdiction. The Centre also submitted that guidelines were already in place for organising protests and that videography was covered under the existing framework. It said the petitioner could make a representation seeking framing of an SOP for the use of body-worn cameras, which could be considered in accordance with law. With the government agreeing to consider the issue as a representation and communicate its decision within six months, the High Court disposed of the PIL. The plea was filed against the backdrop of clashes during the July protests at Jantar Mantar, which resulted in injuries to student protesters as well as more than 50 police and paramilitary personnel. According to the petition, the events exposed a "systemic vacuum" as there was no rule, regulation, standing order or SOP mandating police or RAF personnel to wear body-worn cameras while deployed on crowd-control duties, or governing the storage, integrity, retention and evidentiary use of such footage. The petitioner said the July 2026 protests had seen allegations of disproportionate use of force by police, while there were also allegations of attacks on police personnel and vandalism by some protesters. It submitted that a contemporaneous and tamper-proof officer's-eye recording could help fix accountability for alleged excesses by the police and also provide authenticated evidence to identify and prosecute persons in the crowd who resorted to violence. The plea further claimed that Delhi Police had itself recognised the need for body-worn cameras during protests as far back as January 2020, but had not translated that recognition into a binding and effective regime. It referred to Delhi Police Standing Order No. L&O/10/2022 concerning regulation of rallies and processions, submitting that the existing framework provides for third-person videography but does not mandate body-worn cameras for personnel engaged in crowd control. The petition also claimed that Delhi Police had floated a tender for procurement of 1,500 body-worn cameras at a total value of around Rs 7.4 crore, while the CRPF had initiated procurement of 480 such cameras for the RAF. The petitioner sought directions for framing and enforcement of a binding SOP mandating compulsory, always-on body-worn cameras for police and RAF personnel deployed on crowd-control and protest-management duties, along with a data-storage, integrity and evidentiary regime governing the footage. --IANS pds/vd

articles.title: Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund gets Cabinet nod, manufacturing firms to get majority allocation
articles.description: The Union Cabinet has approved a Rs 10,000 crore government commitment towards setting up an SME Growth Fund (SGF), aimed at providing growth equity to SME seeking to expand their businesses. The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Under the plan, the Government of India will commit an aggregate Rs 10,000 crore to an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) established under the SGF framework. The fund , announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, is intended to address what the government describes as a structural gap in the availability of equity capital for SME. Existing funds provide equity support to businesses, but the government said many are focused on early-stage enterprises and predominantly cover micro enterprises. Majority allocation to manufacturing SMEs A majority of the SGF's allocation will be directed towards SME focused on manufacturing. The fund will provide what the government calls “patient growth equity capital” to high-potential SMEs that have demonstrated business viability and the ability to scale. The government said long-term risk capital is needed by companies looking to expand, adopt advanced technologies, enter international markets, undertake acquisitions and grow into larger businesses. The SGF is intended to provide capital that can help SMEs expand operations, invest in technology and manufacturing capacity, enter overseas markets, integrate into global value chains and undertake strategic investments . It will also consider SMEs operating in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. The government expects investment in these clusters to support regional industrial development, strengthen local supply chains and generate employment. Fund seeks to address growth-stage financing gap The government said that while measures have improved access to credit for SMEs, a gap remains in the availability of long-term risk capital for businesses that have moved beyond their early stages and are seeking further growth. The SGF has been designed to address this gap through equity investment in businesses with demonstrated viability and scalability. Apart from manufacturing, the initiative will cover enterprises operating in services, technology, innovation-driven sectors and strategic value chains. For manufacturing businesses, the government expects the fund to support capacity expansion and technology adoption, while improving productivity and export competitiveness as companies achieve greater scale. SMEs are significant contributors to India's employment, exports, manufacturing output and innovation, making access to growth capital an important issue for companies seeking to expand beyond their existing operations. Part of wider MSME support measures The SME Growth Fund was proposed in the Union Budget 2026-27 as part of measures to provide equity, liquidity and professional support to the wider MSME ecosystem. The government said the initiative will complement measures including credit-support mechanisms, digitalisation programmes, ease-of-doing-business reforms, public procurement reforms, startup promotion initiatives and production-linked incentive schemes. It expects the fund to help develop a pipeline of Indian companies with the scale, innovation capabilities and competitiveness required to become leading businesses in their respective sectors. The initiative has also been linked to the government's Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, including efforts to deepen India's domestic capital market for growth-stage businesses and build companies capable of competing internationally. “By catalysing investment in high-growth SMEs, the Fund will help create champions, drive innovation-led industrialization, and generate quality employment opportunities,” the government said.

articles.title: Approves Rs 10,000-cr SME Growth Fund
articles.description: New Delhi, Oct 6: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Tuesday approved the government’s commitment of Rs 10,000 crore towards the establishment of the SME Growth Fund (SGF) to provide direct equity investments to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and help create a new generation of Indian companies capable of competing globally. The initiative is part of the measures announced in the Union Budget 2026-27 to provide equity, liquidity and professional support to the MSME ecosystem. The government said existing funds provide equity support to enterprises, but most focus on early-stage businesses and largely cover micro enterprises. A structural gap, it said, remains in the availability of growth-stage equity capital for small and medium enterprises. The SGF is aimed at catalysing growth-oriented capital for SMEs across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors and strategic value chains. The government said the initiative would address the financing gap faced by viable SMEs seeking to scale operations, innovate, expand internationally, adopt advanced technologies, undertake acquisitions and emerge as industry leaders. The fund will provide “patient growth equity capital” to high-potential SMEs with demonstrated business viability and scalability. A majority of the fund’s allocation will be directed towards small and medium manufacturing-focused enterprises. It will also consider SMEs operating in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. By providing long-term capital, the initiative is expected to help Indian SMEs expand capacity, adopt advanced technologies, enter international markets, integrate into global value chains and undertake strategic investments. The government said the fund would help create a strong pipeline of Indian companies with the scale, innovation capabilities and competitiveness required to become champions in their respective sectors. Under the initiative, the Government of India will provide an aggregate commitment of Rs 10,000 crore to an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) established under the SGF framework. The government said the fund would complement existing measures to strengthen the SME sector, including digitalisation initiatives, credit support mechanisms, ease of doing business reforms, public procurement reforms, startup promotion initiatives and production-linked incentive programmes. The SGF is also expected to support balanced regional industrial development by investing in industrial clusters, including those in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. Such investments, the government said, would strengthen local supply chains and generate quality employment opportunities. The initiative is part of the government’s broader effort to strengthen India’s entrepreneurship ecosystem, deepen the domestic capital market for growth-stage enterprises and advance the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

articles.title: Cabinet okays Rs10,000 cr SME growth fund
articles.description: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday allocated Rs10,000 crore to establish an SME Growth Fund (SGF) for direct investments in small and medium enterprises (SMEs).The fund, announced in the Union Budget 2026-27, is introduced with the aim of providing growth-oriented capital for SMEs and creating champion enterprises across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors, and strategic value chains. It will also consider SMEs operating in industrial clusters in Tier-II and Tier-III cities.The SGF is intended to address a gap in growth-stage equity financing for SMEs. Existing funds providing equity support largely focus on early-stage businesses and micro enterprises, the government said.Also Read: Tata Sons chairman outlines three steps for sustained economic growthIt will provide long-term capital to businesses with established operations and the potential to scale. The government expects the investments to help SMEs expand their manufacturing capacity, improve productivity, increase exports and participate in global supply chains.The government has also highlighted credit support, digitalisation, public procurement reforms, startup initiatives and production-linked incentive schemes as part of its broader measures for the MSME sector. The official release said the initiative will help SMEs scale operations, and invest in technology and manufacturing capacity.The government has previously introduced a slew of measures as well to help the SMEs. The PM Mudra Yojana (PMMY), introduced in 2015, offers institutional loans of up to Rs20 lakh for non-corporate, non-farm small and micro enterprises. The Trade Receivables e-Discounting System (TReDS), launched in 2017, is an online invoice-discounting platform that helps SMEs convert trade receivables into liquid cash.In another announcement, the Cabinet approved the setting up of an Integrated Transport & Logistics Authority (ITLA) as a Special Purpose Vehicle to strengthen "research, planning, appraisal, monitoring and impact assessment" across transportation and logistics.ITLA will operate as the ‘apex body for integrated transport and logistics planning, research, project appraisal and monitoring, policy support and data analytics’. It will prepare a comprehensive National Transport Master Plan with a planning horizon of 10 years or more, covering roads, railways, shipping and mobility.
